title: EstateMap spec file
description: One YAML file per domain. Every business rule the system enforces lives here, and every rule marked as implemented must point at the code that enforces it.

version.description: Spec format version. Bump only with a matching change in tools/specs/.

domain.description: Domain slug. Must match the file name (properties.yaml -> properties).

status.description: Status of the domain as a whole. A not_implemented domain may only hold proposed rules.

see_also.description: Relative paths to related docs or specs.

catalog.description: Vocabularies this file declares for the rest of the specs. Anything a rule references must be declared in some catalog, which is what stops typos from silently becoming new concepts.

status.description: implemented: the code enforces it today, evidence required. partial: enforced only in some layers, evidence required. proposed/not_implemented: no code exists, evidence forbidden, tests are generated as skipped. deprecated: was enforced, no longer is.

evidence.description: A pointer to the code that enforces the rule. Validated: the file must exist and the line range must be inside it, so moving or deleting the code breaks CI.

symbol.description: Function, class or setting name. Validated as a literal substring of the file, so a rename breaks CI.

case.description: An executable example. tools/specs/gen_tests.py turns these into real tests when there is enough information, and into traceability stubs when there is not.

given.description: The state of the world before the request, never the request itself: 'given a listing already marked as sold'. Executable cases materialise it through SpecWorld.apply in backend/real_estate/tests/spec_support.py, which refuses any key it does not know how to build — a case cannot claim a precondition nobody sets up. The request body goes in 'body'.

body.description: The request body sent to the endpoint. Only meaningful for methods that carry one (POST, PUT, PATCH); declaring it on a GET or DELETE is an error the test harness raises.

endpoint.description: Overrides backend.endpoint for this case. For rules whose statement genuinely spans two routes, e.g. 'the listing resolves by its id and by its short code'.

expected.description: allowed / denied for permission rules, a literal value for calculations, or an object for richer assertions.

expected_http_status.description: For 'allowed' cases, the exact status the call must return. Without it, 'allowed' only proves the request was not refused on permission grounds — a 400 or a 404 would pass. Set it whenever a valid request body can be built.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across every spec file. Never reuse an id.

summary.description: One sentence, in Spanish, stating the rule as a fact.

evidence.description: Required when status is implemented or partial. Forbidden when status is proposed or not_implemented.

conditions.description: Preconditions under which the rule applies.

required.description: Permission slugs. Each must be declared in specs/permissions/matrix.yaml.

routes.description: Next.js routes where the rule is visible to the user.

test_id.description: data-testid used by the Playwright test for this rule.

tests.description: Which layers must cover this rule. The validator enforces that every requested layer has a test tagged SPEC:<id>.
